use_case: A self-hosted web control center where a developer starts and watches coding-agent conversations (OpenHands, or Claude Code/Codex/Gemini over ACP) that edit and run code in their project folders, and sets up scheduled or webhook-triggered automations (e.g. GitHub issue triage, Slack reports).
not_for: This repo is only the React/TypeScript frontend (Agent Canvas); the agent loop, tool implementations and system prompts live in OpenHands/software-agent-sdk (Agent Server)
Not a headless or batch benchmark runner; you drive it through a browser UI backed by an Agent Server
No specialised data/SQL, science or document tooling beyond a general terminal, file editor and browser
evidence: In README.md (lines 7-46, 124-150), the project calls itself a "self-hosted developer control center for coding agents and automations" on top of the OpenHands Agent Server, with ACP agents and Slack/GitHub/Linear automations. In src/api/agent-server-adapter.ts, the default tools are terminal, file_editor and task_tracker (line 145). browser_tool_set and task_tool_set (sub-agents) can be turned on (lines 146-147, 739-766), and a max_iterations default of 500 is set (line 150). Planning agents use glob, grep, a plan file editor and system_prompt_planning.j2 with a condenser (lines 1430-1459). AGENTS.md says the agent/tools/prompts are owned by software-agent-sdk.
